commentaries.whitney: Whence the sun arises, and where he goes to rest—that same I think the chief ( jyeṣṭhá ); that nothing whatever surpasses.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The Kaṭha Up. ⌊iv. 9⌋ has a nearly corresponding verse: yataç co ’d eti sūryo “staṁ yatra ca gacchati: taṁ devāḥ sarve ‘rpitās tad u nā ’ty eti kaç cana; and the first half of this occurs also in ÇB. xiv. 4. 3 34 (BAU. i. 5. 23). The Anukr. omits to define the meter ( anuṣṭubh ) of the verse.

commentaries.whitney: They who hitherward, in the middle, or also anciently, speak round about him who knows the Veda, they all speak around the sun ( ādityá ), Agni [as] second, and the threefold swan ( haṅsá ).
commentaries.whitney_notes: The verse is found also in TA. (ii. 15 8 ), which omits mádhye and reads purāṇé in a , and tṛtī́yam (for trivṛ́tam ) in d . ⌊Cf. Kaṭha-hss. , p. 63.⌋ Our pada -text ⌊as also SPP's⌋ reads near the beginning arvā́n̄ , which is doubtless an error for arvā́k (though TA. reads arvā́n̄ utá ). Perhaps védam in b is to be rendered simply 'knowledge.' The Anukr. takes no notice of the two redundant syllables in c .

commentaries.whitney: A thousand days' journey [are] expanded ( vi-yam ) the wings of him, of the yellow swan flying to heaven ( svargá ); he, putting all the gods in his breast, goes, viewing together all existences.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The verse is found again below as xiii. 2. 38; 3. 14. It is, as noted above, wanting here in Ppp.

commentaries.whitney: Whoever indeed knows those two churning-sticks, with which is churned out what is good ( vásu ), he may think himself to know the chief thing; he may know the great bráhmaṇa ⌊neut.⌋.

commentaries.whitney: Footless came he into being in the beginning; he in the beginning brought the heaven ( svàr ); having become four-footed, enjoyable, he took to himself all enjoyment ( bhójana ),
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads, for b , so ‘gre asurā ’bhavat .

commentaries.whitney_notes: ⌊After bhógyo bhavat , for which there are no variants, Bp. has a mark of pāda-division; but the Anukr. evidently scans as 12: 8 + 8, eliding the a of ánnam after a pragṛhya .⌋ Bhā́gyo at the beginning is a misprint for bhógyo .

commentaries.whitney: Everlasting they call him, also may he be at present ever-renewed; day and night are generated ( pra-jā ) in each other's forms.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The pada -text reads anyáḥ: anyásya in d , although the masc. anyás shows that the two words are virtually a compound, as later.

commentaries.whitney: A hundred, a thousand, a myriad, a hundred million, an innumerable [number], is his own entered into him; that of him they slay, even as he looks on; therefore this god shines ( ruc ) thus.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Instead of eṣa etat at the end, Ppp. reads what appears to be agha bhavat . The version is as literal (and as unintelligent) as possible. The Anukr. takes no notice of the irregularity of the meter; it is possible, by violence, to count only 44 syllables in the verse.

commentaries.whitney: One thing is more minute ( áṇu ) than a child ( bā́la ), also one is hardly ( né ’va ) seen; than that a more embracing deity, is she dear to me.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads, for a , ārāgramātraṁ dadṛçe , and begins c with ataṣ pa- , thus doing nothing to help our comprehension of the wholly obscure verse.

commentaries.whitney: This beautiful one (f.) [is] unaging, an immortal in the house of a mortal; for whom she [was] made, he lies; he who made [her] grew old.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads tasmāi for yasmāi in c . ⌊The natural reading of b would be mártyasya amṛ́ta gṛhé ; but⌋ the definition of the Anukr. forbids us to make ⌊it. Can a sā́ have dropped out before çáye sá? Cf. note to iv. 5. 5.⌋

items.samhita_patha: त्वं स्त्री त्वं पुमा॑नसि॒ त्वं कु॑मा॒र उ॒त वा॑ कुमा॒री। त्वं जी॒र्णो द॒ण्डेन॑ वञ्चसि॒ त्वं जा॒तो भ॑वसि वि॒श्वतो॑मुखः ॥

commentaries.whitney: Thou art woman, thou [art] man, thou boy, or also girl; thou, when aged, totterest ( vañc ) with a staff; thou, when born, becomest facing all ways.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. politely puts kumārī first and kumāras second in b , and reads jātam in d . The verse is found, without variant, in Çvet. Up. iv. 3. It is so far correctly described by the Anukr. that it counts 37 syllables (7 + 10: 9 + 11 = 37).

items.samhita_patha: उ॒तैषां॑ पि॒तोत वा॑ पु॒त्र ए॑षामु॒तैषां॑ ज्ये॒ष्ठ उ॒त वा॑ कनि॒ष्ठः। एको॑ ह दे॒वो मन॑सि॒ प्रवि॑ष्टः प्रथ॒मो जा॒तः स उ॒ गर्भे॑ अ॒न्तः ॥

commentaries.whitney: Both their father, or also their son; both the chief or also the meanest ( kaniṣṭhá ) of them; the one god, who has entered into the mind, born the first, and he within the womb.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The verse is also found, quoted as a çloka , in JUB. 85 (iii. 10. 12): utāi ’ṣāṁ jāiṣṭha uta vā kaniṣṭha utāi ’ṣāṁ putra uta vā pitāi ’ṣāṁ: eko ha devo manasi praviṣṭaḥ pūrvo ha jajñe sa u garbhe ‘ntaḥ . Ppp. reads, for a, b , ute ’va jyeṣṭho ’ta vā kaniṣṭho ’tāi ’ṣa bhrāto ’ta vā pitāi ’ṣaḥ; and, in d , pūrvo jātaḥ .

commentaries.whitney: The full from the full he bends up ( ud-ac ); the full is poured with the full; also that may we know today, whence that is poured out.
commentaries.whitney_notes: This verse is akin with ⌊the oft-repeated⌋ one in ÇB. xiv. 8. 1 (BAU. v. 1): pūrṇám adáḥ pūrṇám idám pūrṇā́t pūrṇám úd acyate etc. What follows of the hymn is (as noted above) wanting in Ppp.

commentaries.whitney: She, everlasting, born indeed of old, she, ancient, encompassed ( pari-bhū ) all; the great goddess of the dawn, shining forth, she looks forth by every one who winks.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The Anukr. calls the verse bhurij on account of the redundant syllable in b , not heeding the corresponding deficiency in c .

items.samhita_patha: अवि॒र्वै नाम॑ दे॒वत॒र्तेना॑स्ते॒ परी॑वृता। तस्या॑ रू॒पेणे॒मे वृ॒क्षा हरि॑ता॒ हरि॑तस्रजः ॥

commentaries.whitney: The deity, Avi by name, sits enveloped with right; by her form these trees [are] green, green-garlanded.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Or, 'by the form of her, the green-garlanded one' (so Ludwig). Ávi means 'sheep,' but is possibly here a derivative from the root av 'favor, aid.' All the saṁhitā -mss. combine in a, b -ta rténa .

commentaries.whitney_notes: There is nothing to determine the subject of the verbs in a, b ; Ludwig renders 'she.'

commentaries.whitney_notes: The Anukr. takes no notice of the redundant syllable ⌊perhaps the first ca? ⌋ in a .

commentaries.whitney: They by whom the wind sent forth blows on, who give the five quarters together ( sadhryàñc ), the gods who thought themselves above ( ati-man ) the offering ( ā́huti ), conductors of the waters—which were they?
commentaries.whitney_notes: The first half-verse is found also in Ppp. ⌊xvi.⌋, but not in connection with the rest of the hymn. The Anukr. does not heed that a is defective by one syllable. Read in b , with all ⌊W's and SPP's⌋ mss., dádante; the form is from the same secondary root dad as the sing. dadate in 36 c . ⌊JUB. (i. 34) has this verse, putting it in the mouth of Pṛthu Vāinya, and its answer (vs. 36), with appended Brāhmaṇa-comment. It reads samīcīḥ for sadhrīcīḥ of our 35 b , and āhutīs in c .⌋

commentaries.whitney_notes: ⌊JUB. (see under vs. 35) has ekas for eṣām of our c and anye for eke of our d .⌋

commentaries.whitney: I know the stretched-out string in which these offspring are woven in; the string of the string I know, likewise the great brā́hmaṇa .

commentaries.whitney: As between heaven-and-earth Agni went, burning on, all-consuming, where stood beyond they (f.) of one husband—where perchance was Mātariçvan then?
commentaries.whitney_notes: The bṛhatī of the Anukr. ⌊scanning 11 + 9: 11 + 11⌋ the second pāda, read with āit included as a part (the pada -text so marks the division)—which is, of course, artificial and wrong. ⌊Read as 12 + 8: 11 + 11, pronouncing -dāvías and kúe ’vā ”sīn .⌋ Ludwig's 'spouses of the only one' for ékapatnīs is against the accent.

commentaries.whitney: Mātariçvan was entered into the waters; the gods were entered into the seas; great stood the traverser of space; the purifying one entered into the green ones.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The third pāda is identical with 3 c above, and the fourth with RV. viii. 90 (101). 14 d . 'The purifying one' is probably here the wind.

commentaries.whitney: Higher, as it were, than the gāyatrī́ , upon the immortal ( amṛ́ta ) he strode out; they who know completely chant with chant—where then was seen the goat?
commentaries.whitney_notes: Or, 'the unborn one' ( ajá: so Ludwig); the verse is too utterly obscure to let us choose between them.

commentaries.whitney: The reposer, the assembler of good things, like god Savitar, of true ordinances ( -dhárman ), he stood like Indra in the conflict for riches.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The verse corresponds with pādas a, c, d of RV. x. 139. 3 and of VS. xii. 66, TS. iv. 2. 5 4 , MS.ii. 7. 12. RV. reads at the beginning rāyó budhnáḥ (for nivéçanaḥ ) the other texts have at the end pathīnā́m . The verse is quoted in Vāit. 28. 28.

commentaries.whitney: The lotus-flower of nine doors, covered with three strands ( guṇá ) — what soulful prodigy ( yakṣá ) is within it, that the bráhman -knowers know.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The 'nine doors' indicate that the human body with its nine orifices is intended; the three guṇas are probably the three temperaments familiar under that name later. The second half-verse was found above as 2. 32 c, d ⌊cf. vs. 31⌋. ⌊☞ See p. 1045.⌋

commentaries.whitney: Free from desire, wise ( dhī́ra ), immortal, self-existent, satisfied with sap, not deficient in any respect—knowing that wise, unaging, young soul, one is not afraid of death.
commentaries.whitney_notes: ⌊See Deussen, Geschichte , i. 1. 334: "die erste und älteste Stelle, die wir kennen, in der rückhaltlos der Ātman als Weltprincip proklamiert wird, AV. x. 8. 44." Cf. also p. 312, end. Muir, Metrical Translations from Sanskrit Writers , p. 1, gives a metrical paraphrase of the verse.⌋ ⌊The quoted Anukr. says caturdaça (i.e. 14 above 30). The fourth anuvāka , with 2 hymns and 88 verses, ends here.⌋

commentaries.whitney: Fasten thou up the mouths of the mischief-making ⌊ones⌋; bring ( arpay- ) this thunderbolt upon our rivals; given by Indra, first, with a hundred rice-dishes, cousin-slaying, the success ( gātú ) of the sacrificer.
commentaries.whitney_notes: It is a cow (f.) accompanied by a whole hundred of odanas or offerings of boiled rice, that is here the subject; we had in various places above a goat (m.) with five such additions. Ppp. reads in d yajamānāya . The Anukr. does not heed that the third pāda is jagatī .

items.samhita_patha_plain: अघायतामपि नह्या मुखानि सपत्नेषु वज्रमर्पयैतम्। इन्द्रेण दत्ता प्रथमा शतौदना भ्रातृव्यघ्नी यजमानस्य गातुः ॥

commentaries.whitney: Be thy skin the sacrificial hearth, [be] the hairs which [are] thine the barhís; this rein ( raçanā́ ) hath seized thee; let this pressing-stone dance over thee.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The parts of this and the preceding verse are prescribed in Kāuc. 65. 1-3 to be used to accompany certain sacrificial acts to which they are adapted.

items.samhita_patha: बाला॑स्ते॒ प्रोक्ष॑णीः सन्तु जि॒ह्वा सं मा॑र्ष्ट्वघ्न्ये। शु॒द्धा त्वं य॒ज्ञिया॑ भू॒त्वा दिवं॒ प्रेहि॑ शतौदने ॥

commentaries.whitney: Be thy tail-tuft the sprinklers; let thy tongue do the cleansing, O inviolable one; do thou, having become clean, fit for sacrifice, go on to heaven, O thou of the hundred rice-dishes.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The form bā́las (which Ppp. also reads) ⌊as against vā́las ⌋ is vouched for ⌊incidentally⌋ by the comm. to Prāt. i. 66 ⌊in its discussion of the exchange of r and l ⌋. The verse is quoted in Kāuç. 65.9. Sam mārṣṭu = 'serve as sammārjana .'

commentaries.whitney: Whoso cooks her of the hundred rice-dishes, he is adapted to the fulfilment of wishes; for all his priests ( ṛtvíj ), being gratified, go as they should.
commentaries.whitney_notes: All the saṁhitā -mss. read in c asya rtv- .

commentaries.whitney: He ascends the heavenly road ( svargá ), where is yon triple heaven of the heaven ( dív ), who, making [her] cake-naveled, gives her of the hundred rice-dishes.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The meaning and connection of c are not very clear. Ludwig renders "and makes her the middle point of the apūpa ," which is against the accent; probably 'adding cakes numerous enough to cover her.' ⌊Is it not virtually equivalent to 'putting a cake on her navel,' as preparatory to sacrificing her?⌋ Ppp. has hiraṇyajyotiṣam instead of apūpanābhim (cf. the next verse). The resolution kṛtu-ā́ , necessary to make the verse a regular anuṣṭubh , is rather harsh.

commentaries.whitney_notes: That is, probably, exceed or surpass even this important ceremony.

commentaries.whitney: The gods, the Fathers, men ( manuṣyà ), and they that are Gandharvas-and-Apsarases—they shall all guard thee; do thou run beyond the over-night sacrifice ( atirātrá ).
commentaries.whitney_notes: Found also in Pāipp. xvi. The hymn (vs. 1) is quoted in Kāuç. 65. 1 to accompany the closing of the mouth of a victim, and some of the verses (1-3, 26, 27) in other neighboring parts of the sūtra. In Vāit. is used a single verse (26). Translated: Ludwig, p. 270 (in great part); Henry, 32, 83; Griffith, ii. 42. Ppp. reads gandharvāpsaraso devā rudrān̄girasas tvā . ⌊Cf. note to vs. 8.⌋

commentaries.whitney_notes: Several of the mss., with a carelessness common in such cases, read dhukṣa in d . We have to resolve deva-ā in a , in order to make a normal pāda. Ppp. rectifies the meter of a by reading instead pitaras for devās . ⌊Ppp. combines -ṣado ‘ntar- in a-b .⌋

commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads in a yāny asthīni , thus rectifying the meter. The Anukr. does not notice the lacking syllable in the pāda. Yás at the beginning is again emendation for the yát of all the mss. ⌊both W's and SPP's⌋.

items.samhita_patha: यास्ते॒ जङ्घा॒ याः कुष्ठि॑का ऋ॒च्छरा॒ ये च॑ ते श॒फाः। आ॒मिक्षां॑ दुह्रतां दा॒त्रे क्षी॒रं स॒र्पिरथो॒ मधु॑ ॥

commentaries.whitney:
What hind-thighs are thine, what dew-claws, [what] pasterns
( ṛchára ), and what thy hoofs—let them yield etc. etc.
commentaries.whitney_notes: One of our mss. (O.) reads in b ṛtsárās , and Ppp. supports it by giving kṛtsarās . ⌊The reading ṛtsárās seems to be supported by E. as well as by O. and Ppp. Its phonetic relation to ṛcchárās resembles that of Pāli ucchādana, jighacchā, bībhaccha to Skt. utsādana, jighatsā, bībhatsa (Kuhn, Pāli-gram. , p. 52, gives kucchā = kutsā, vaccha = vatsa ). Unless I err, our vulgate text here shows a Prākritism such as we have good right to assume also at iii. 12. 4, in case of the much-discussed ucchántu , which may be a mere vernacularized rendering of ukṣántu (cf. tacchaka = takṣaka , Kuhn, l.c.).⌋

items.samhita_patha: क्रो॒डौ ते॑ स्तां पुरो॒डाशा॒वाज्ये॑ना॒भिघा॑रितौ। तौ प॒क्षौ दे॑वि कृ॒त्वा सा प॒क्तारं॒ दिवं॑ वह ॥

commentaries.whitney: Let thy two breasts ( kroḍá ) be sacrificial cakes, smeared over with sacrificial butter; having made them wings, O divine one, do thou carry him who cooks thee to heaven ( dív ).
commentaries.whitney_notes: The Anukr. very strangely ignores the two resolutions in b and c , and reckons the pādas as 7 syllables each.

items.samhita_patha: उ॒लूख॑ले॒ मुस॑ले॒ यश्च॒ चर्म॑णि॒ यो वा॒ शूर्पे॑ तण्डु॒लः कणः॑। यं वा॒ वातो॑ मात॒रिश्वा॒ पव॑मानो म॒माथा॒ग्निष्टद्धोता॒ सुहु॑तं कृणोतु ॥

commentaries.whitney: What in the mortar, on the pestle, and on the hide, or what rice-grain, [what] kernel in the winnowing-basket, or what the wind, Mātariçvan, blowing ( pū ), shook ( math )—let Agni as hótar make that well-offered.
commentaries.whitney_notes: It is very much out of place to reckon five pādas (12 + 9: 8 + 7 + 11 = 47) in this verse; but the pada -ms. supports the Anukr., by making a mark of pāda-division after mātaríçvā; evidently either this word or pávamānas (rather the former) is an intrusion in c . ⌊The last pāda we had as vi. 71. 1 d .⌋ The verse is quoted in Vāit. 4. 9; also (with vi. 122, 123) in Kāuç. 63. 29, to accompany the closing libations. Ppp. reads in b ye vā çūrpe taṇḍulāṣ kaṇāḥ .

commentaries.whitney: The heavenly waters, rich in honey, dripping with ghee, I seat in separate succession in the hands of the priests ( brahmán ); with what desire I now pour you on, let all that fall to my lot; may we be lords of wealth.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. begins a with imā āpo madh- , and c with yatkāme ’dam . Compare the verses vi. 122. 5 and xi. 1. 27, which are in part coincident with this; ⌊also MGS. i. 5. 4 and Index under devīr āpo . The verse (rather than i. 4. 3, which has the same pratīka ) is quoted in Kāuç. 65. 8, to accompany the setting of water pots. The metrical definition of the Anukr. suits well enough. ⌊The quoted Anukr. says " aghāyatām ": cf . vs. 1.⌋

commentaries.whitney_notes: The Anukr. chooses to reject the common resolution -bhi-as (twice) in c .

commentaries.whitney: By whom the sky, by whom the earth, by whom these waters are guarded—the cow, of a thousand streams ( -dhā́rā ), we address with worship ( bráhman ).
commentaries.whitney_notes: We need to resolve -dhāra-ām in c in order to make out the full pāda which the Anukr. assumes.

items.samhita_patha_plain: यया द्यौर्यया पृथिवी ययापो गुपिता इमाः। वशां सहस्रधारां ब्रह्मणाच्छावदामसि ॥

items.samhita_patha: श॒तं कं॒साः श॒तं दो॒ग्धारः॑ श॒तं गो॒प्तारो॒ अधि॑ पृ॒ष्ठे अ॑स्याः। ये दे॒वास्तस्यां॑ प्रा॒णन्ति॑ ते व॒शां वि॑दुरेक॒धा ॥

commentaries.whitney: A hundred metal dishes ( kaṅsá ), a hundred milkers, a hundred guardians, upon the back of her; the gods that breathe in her, they know the cow singly.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The verse (9 + 11: 8 + 8 = 36) is a bṛhatī in number of syllables only.

commentaries.whitney: Having the sacrifice for feet, cheer ( írā- ) for milk, svadhā́ for breath, being mahī́lukā , the cow, having Parjanya for spouse, goes unto the gods with worship ( bráhman ).
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads for a, b yajñapatir ākṣīrāt svadhāprāṇā mahilokāḥ , which does not solve the problem of the obscure word mahī́lukā (found nowhere else). There is no need of calling the verse virāj .

items.samhita_patha_plain: यज्ञपदीराक्षीरा स्वधाप्राणा महीलुका। वशा पर्जन्यपत्नी देवाँ अप्येति ब्रह्मणा ॥

items.samhita_patha: अनु॑ त्वा॒ग्निः प्रावि॑श॒दनु॒ सोमो॑ वशे त्वा। ऊध॑स्ते भद्रे प॒र्जन्यो॑ वि॒द्युत॑स्ते॒ स्तना॑ वशे ॥

commentaries.whitney: After thee entered Agni, after thee Soma, O cow; thine udder, O excellent one, is Parjanya; the lightnings are thy teats, O cow.

items.samhita_patha_plain: अनु त्वाग्निः प्राविशदनु सोमो वशे त्वा। ऊधस्ते भद्रे पर्जन्यो विद्युतस्ते स्तना वशे ॥

items.samhita_patha: अ॒पस्त्वं धु॑क्षे प्रथ॒मा उ॒र्वरा॒ अप॑रा वशे। तृ॒तीयं॑ रा॒ष्ट्रं धु॒क्षेऽन्नं॑ क्षी॒रं व॑शे॒ त्वम् ॥

commentaries.whitney: The waters thou yieldest ( duh ) first, the cultivated fields after, O cow; thou yieldest kingdom third, food, milk, O cow.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The permissible resolution rāṣ-ṭṛ-ám in c would obviate the necessity of reckoning the verse as virāj . Ppp. combines in b urvarā ’parā .

items.samhita_patha_plain: अपस्त्वं धुक्षे प्रथमा उर्वरा अपरा वशे। तृतीयं राष्ट्रं धुक्षेऽन्नं क्षीरं वशे त्वम् ॥

commentaries.whitney: When, called by the Ādityas, thou didst approach, O righteous one, Indra made thee drink a thousand vessels ( pā́tra ) of soma, O cow.
commentaries.whitney_notes: By a notable inconsistency, the Anukr. reckons this verse as a complete anuṣṭubh , although it requires, to make it such, precisely the same resolution ( pā́-tṛ-ān ) as vs. 8.

commentaries.whitney: When thou didst go following ( anváñc ) Indra, then the bull called thee; therefore the Vṛitra-slayer, angry, took thy milk ( páyas ), milk ( kṣīrá ), O cow.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Found also in Pāipp. xvi. ⌊with the verse-sequence 15 a, b , 14 c, d , 13, 14 a, b , 15 c, d , 17, 16, 18; vs. 3 is lacking⌋. Not noticed in Vāit., and only once in Kāuç., at 66. 20, where vs. 1 (or the hymn ⌊rather the hymn⌋) is used, with xii. 4, to accompany the sprinkling of an offered cow. Translated: Ludwig, p. 534; Deussen, Geschichte , i. 1. 234 (cf. p. 230 f., 233 f.); Henry, 35, 85; Griffith, ii. 45. All the saṁhitā -mss. accent in b -bhó ‘hvayat , and one. pada -ms. (D.) has accordingly áhvayat . In like manner, all save R.p.m. have kruddhó ‘har- in d . In both cases our edition emends to ò . In this verse also (as in 6, 8) the designation virāj is uncalled-for. Ppp. reads uvūcī in a , and ād vṛṣabho in b .

commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads, in a-b , -patiḥ kṣīraṁ dehi bharad vaçe .

commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads hitaṁ for tam in a , and ādyevy abharad in b .

commentaries.whitney_notes: Before this verse, Ppp. sets one made up of our 15 a, b and 14 c, d . Pada -text in c ádhi: asthāt . ⌊As to kali , cf. Bergaigne, Rel. Véd. ii. 482.⌋ ⌊For ágata , see Gram. §834 b .⌋

commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. combines (as above noted) our 15 a, b and 14 c, d , and then again our 14 a, b and 15 c, d , without other variant.

commentaries.whitney_notes: Some of the mss. (P.M.E.) read in c aty akṣad (K. akṣyad ).

commentaries.whitney: As, O righteous one, thou didst stand decked ( abhi-vṛ ) with gold, the ocean, having become a horse, mounted ( adhi-skand ) thee, O cow.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. puts this verse after our 17.

items.samhita_patha_plain: अभीवृता हिरण्येन यदतिष्ठ ऋतावरि। अश्वः समुद्रो भूत्वाध्यस्कन्दद्वशे त्वा ॥

items.samhita_patha: तद्भ॒द्राः सम॑गच्छन्त व॒शा देष्ट्र्यथो॑ स्व॒धा। अथ॑र्वा॒ यत्र॑ दीक्षि॒तो ब॒र्हिष्यास्त॑ हिर॒ण्यये॑ ॥

commentaries.whitney: There the excellent ones united, the cow, the directress, also the svadhā́ , where Atharvan, consecrated, sat on a golden barhís .
commentaries.whitney_notes: The second half-verse is identical with 12 c, d above. Ppp. reads in a gachanti .

items.samhita_patha_plain: तद्भद्राः समगच्छन्त वशा देष्ट्र्यथो स्वधा। अथर्वा यत्र दीक्षितो बर्हिष्यास्त हिरण्यये ॥

items.samhita_patha: व॒शा मा॒ता रा॑ज॒न्य᳡स्य व॒शा मा॒ता स्व॑धे॒ तव॑। व॒शाया॑ य॒ज्ञ आयु॑धं॒ तत॑श्चि॒त्तम॑जायत ॥

commentaries.whitney: The cow is mother of the noble ( rājanyà ), the cow thy mother, O svadhā́; from the cow was born the weapon; from it was born intent ( cittá ).
commentaries.whitney_notes: The translation implies the obvious emendation of yajñé in c to jajñé , as at iv. 24. 6 ⌊see note thereto⌋.

items.samhita_patha_plain: वशा माता राजन्य᳡स्य वशा माता स्वधे तव। वशाया यज्ञ आयुधं ततश्चित्तमजायत ॥

items.samhita_patha: ऊ॒र्ध्वो बि॒न्दुरुद॑चर॒द्ब्रह्म॑णः॒ ककु॑दा॒दधि॑। तत॒स्त्वं ज॑ज्ञिषे वशे॒ ततो॒ होता॑जायत ॥

commentaries.whitney: The globule ( bindú ) went ( car ) up aloft, out of the summit ( kákuda ) of the bráhman; thence wast thou born, O cow; thence was the invoker born.

items.samhita_patha_plain: ऊर्ध्वो बिन्दुरुदचरद्ब्रह्मणः ककुदादधि। ततस्त्वं जज्ञिषे वशे ततो होताजायत ॥

items.samhita_patha: आ॒स्नस्ते॒ गाथा॑ अभवन्नु॒ष्णिहा॑भ्यो॒ बलं॑ वशे। पा॑ज॒स्या᳡ज्जज्ञे य॒ज्ञ स्तने॑भ्यो र॒श्मय॒स्तव॑ ॥

commentaries.whitney: From thy mouth came ( bhū ) the songs ( gā́thā ), from thy nape-bones, O cow, [came] force; from thy belly (? pājasyà ) was born the sacrifice, from thy teats the rays.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads in a bhavanti for abhavan .

items.samhita_patha_plain: आस्नस्ते गाथा अभवन्नुष्णिहाभ्यो बलं वशे। पाजस्या᳡ज्जज्ञे यज्ञ स्तनेभ्यो रश्मयस्तव ॥

items.samhita_patha: ई॒र्माभ्या॒मय॑नं जा॒तं सक्थि॑भ्यां च वशे॒ तव॑। आ॒न्त्रेभ्यो॑ जज्ञिरे अ॒त्रा उ॒दरा॒दधि॑ वी॒रुधः॑ ॥

commentaries.whitney: From thy (two) fore-legs ( īrmá ) motion ( áyana ) was born, and from thy thighs ( sákthi ), O cow; from thine entrails were born eaters ( attrá ), out from thy belly ( udára ) the plants.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads at the beginning ayurmābhyām , and in c yatrā jajñire . ⌊For atrā́s , cf. note to i. 7. 3.⌋

items.samhita_patha_plain: ईर्माभ्यामयनं जातं सक्थिभ्यां च वशे तव। आन्त्रेभ्यो जज्ञिरे अत्रा उदरादधि वीरुधः ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: ईर्माभ्याम्‌ । अयनम् । जातम् । सक्थिऽभ्याम् । च । वशे । तव । आन्त्रेभ्य: । जज्ञिरे । अत्रा: । उदरात् । अधि । वीरुध: ॥१०.२१॥

items.samhita_patha: यदु॒दरं॒ वरु॑ण॒स्यानु॒प्रावि॑शथा वशे। तत॑स्त्वा ब्र॒ह्मोद॑ह्वय॒त्स हि ने॒त्रमवे॒त्तव॑ ॥

commentaries.whitney: When ( yát ), O cow, thou didst enter along the belly of Varuṇa, thence the priest ( brahmán ) called thee up; for he knew thy guidance ( netrá ).

items.samhita_patha_plain: यदुदरं वरुणस्यानुप्राविशथा वशे। ततस्त्वा ब्रह्मोदह्वयत्स हि नेत्रमवेत्तव ॥

items.samhita_patha: सर्वे॒ गर्भा॑दवेपन्त॒ जाय॑मानादसू॒स्वः᳡। स॒सूव॒ हि तामा॒हुर्व॒शेति॒ ब्रह्म॑भिः॒ क्लृप्तः स ह्य᳡स्या॒ बन्धुः॑ ॥

commentaries.whitney: All trembled at the embryo, while being born, of her who gives not birth (? asūsū́ ); for "the cow hath given birth," they say of her; shaped (m.) by charms ( bráhman ); for it is her connection.

items.samhita_patha_plain: सर्वे गर्भादवेपन्त जायमानादसूस्वः᳡। ससूव हि तामाहुर्वशेति ब्रह्मभिः क्लृप्तः स ह्य᳡स्या बन्धुः ॥

items.samhita_patha: युध॒ एकः॒ सं सृ॑जति॒ यो अ॑स्या॒ एक॒ इद्व॒शी। तरां॑सि य॒ज्ञा अ॑भव॒न्तर॑सां॒ चक्षु॑रभवद्व॒शा ॥

commentaries.whitney: One combines ( sam-sṛj ) the fighters who alone is in control ( vaçín ) of her; the sacrifices became energies (? táras ); the cow became the eye of energies.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The Anukr. should have qualified the name of this bṛhatī by adding virāj . Ppp. combines at the beginning yudhe ’kas s- .

items.samhita_patha_plain: युध एकः सं सृजति यो अस्या एक इद्वशी। तरांसि यज्ञा अभवन्तरसां चक्षुरभवद्वशा ॥

items.samhita_patha: व॒शा य॒ज्ञं प्रत्य॑गृह्णाद्व॒शा सूर्य॑मधारयत्। व॒शाया॑म॒न्तर॑विशदोद॒नो ब्र॒ह्मणा॑ स॒ह ॥

commentaries.whitney: The cow accepted the sacrifice; the cow sustained the sun; within the cow entered the rice-dish together with the priest ( brahmán ).
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads yajñam instead of sūryam in b . All the mss. have brahmáṇā .

items.samhita_patha_plain: वशा यज्ञं प्रत्यगृह्णाद्वशा सूर्यमधारयत्। वशायामन्तरविशदोदनो ब्रह्मणा सह ॥

items.samhita_patha: व॒शामे॒वामृत॑माहुर्व॒शां मृ॒त्युमुपा॑सते। व॒शेदं सर्व॑मभवद्दे॒वा म॑नु॒ष्या॒ असु॑राः पि॒तर॒ ऋष॑यः ॥

commentaries.whitney: The cow they call immortality ( amṛ́ta ); the cow they worship ( upa-ās ) as death; the cow became this all—gods, men, Asuras, Fathers, seers.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads āhur amṛtaṁ in a . The definition of the meter by the Anukr. is bad; it ⌊seems to be 8 + 8: 8 + 14⌋.

items.samhita_patha_plain: वशामेवामृतमाहुर्वशां मृत्युमुपासते। वशेदं सर्वमभवद्देवा मनुष्या असुराः पितर ऋषयः ॥

commentaries.whitney: Whoso knoweth thus, he may accept the cow; for so doth the all-footed sacrifice yield milk ( duh ) to the giver, unresisting.

items.samhita_patha_plain: य एवं विद्यात्स वशां प्रति गृह्णीयात्। तथा हि यज्ञः सर्वपाद्दुहे दात्रेऽनपस्फुरन् ॥

items.samhita_patha: ति॒स्रो जि॒ह्वा वरु॑णस्या॒न्तर्दी॑द्यत्या॒सनि॑। तासां॒ या मध्ये॒ राज॑ति॒ सा व॒शा दु॑ष्प्रति॒ग्रहा॑ ॥

commentaries.whitney: Three tongues glisten ( dīdī ) within the mouth of Varuṇa; of these, the one that shines ( rāj ) in the middle is the cow, hard of acceptance.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The mss., as is usual in such cases, are divided between duḥpr- and duṛpr- in d .

items.samhita_patha_plain: तिस्रो जिह्वा वरुणस्यान्तर्दीद्यत्यासनि। तासां या मध्ये राजति सा वशा दुष्प्रतिग्रहा ॥

items.samhita_patha: च॑तु॒र्धा रेतो॑ अभवद्व॒शायाः॑। आप॒स्तुरी॑यम॒मृतं॒ तुरी॑यं य॒ज्ञस्तुरी॑यं प॒शव॒स्तुरी॑यम् ॥

commentaries.whitney: The seed of the cow was quartered: the waters a quarter, the amṛ́ta a quarter, the sacrifice a quarter, the domestic animals a quarter.

items.samhita_patha_plain: चतुर्धा रेतो अभवद्वशायाः। आपस्तुरीयममृतं तुरीयं यज्ञस्तुरीयं पशवस्तुरीयम् ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: चतु:ऽधा । रेत: । अभवत् । वशाया: । आप: । तुरीयम् । अमृतम् । तुरीयम् । यज्ञ: । तुरीयम् । पशव: । तुरीयम् ॥१०.२९॥

items.samhita_patha: व॒शा द्यौर्व॒शा पृ॑थि॒वी व॒शा विष्णुः॑ प्र॒जाप॑तिः। व॒शाया॑ दु॒ग्धम॑पिबन्त्सा॒ध्या वस॑वश्च ये ॥

commentaries.whitney: The cow [is] the sky, the cow the earth, the cow Vishṇu, Prajāpati; the yield ( dugdhá ) of the cow did the Perfectibles ( sādhyá ) and they who are Vasus drink.

items.samhita_patha_plain: वशा द्यौर्वशा पृथिवी वशा विष्णुः प्रजापतिः। वशाया दुग्धमपिबन्त्साध्या वसवश्च ये ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: वशा । द्यौ: । वशा । पृथिवी । वशा । विष्णु: । प्रजाऽपति: । वशाया: । दुग्धम् । अपिबन् । साध्या: । वसव: । च । ये ॥१०.३०॥

items.samhita_patha: व॒शाया॑ दु॒ग्धं पी॒त्वा सा॒ध्या वस॑वश्च ये। ते वै ब्र॒ध्नस्य॑ वि॒ष्टपि॒ पयो॑ अस्या॒ उपा॑सते ॥

commentaries.whitney: Having drunk the yield of the cow, the Perfectibles and they who are Vasus—they verily worship the milk ( páyas ) of her at the summit of the ruddy one.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads ime instead of te vāi at beginning of c . The definition of the meter by the Anukr. is bad, the verse being, by usual and easy resolutions, a regular anuṣṭubh .

items.samhita_patha_plain: वशाया दुग्धं पीत्वा साध्या वसवश्च ये। ते वै ब्रध्नस्य विष्टपि पयो अस्या उपासते ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: वशाया: । दुग्धम् । पीत्वा । साध्या: । वसव: । च । ये । ते । वै । ब्रध्नस्य । विष्टपि । पय: । अस्या: । उप । आसते ॥१०.३१॥

items.samhita_patha: सोम॑मेना॒मेके॑ दुह्रे घृ॒तमेक॒ उपा॑सते। य ए॒वं वि॒दुषे॑ व॒शां द॒दुस्ते॑ ग॒तास्त्रि॑दि॒वं दि॒वः ॥

commentaries.whitney: Some milk her for soma; some worship ghee; they who gave the cow to the one knowing thus are gone to the triple heaven of the heaven.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The pada -mss., by an absurd blunder, read yā́ before evám into yáḥ instead of yé . It is apparently the intrusion of vaçā́m into c that makes the meter irregular. ⌊Pādas a, b are a reminiscence of RV. x. 154. 1 (= AV. xviii. 2. 14).⌋

items.samhita_patha_plain: सोममेनामेके दुह्रे घृतमेक उपासते। य एवं विदुषे वशां ददुस्ते गतास्त्रिदिवं दिवः ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: सोमम् । एनाम् । एके । दुह्रे । घृतम् । एके । उप । आसते । ये । एवम् । विदुषे । वशाम् । ददु: । ते । गता: । त्रिऽदिवम् । दिव: ॥१०.३२॥

items.samhita_patha: ब्रा॑ह्म॒णेभ्यो॑ व॒शां द॒त्त्वा सर्वां॑ल्लो॒कान्त्सम॑श्नुते। ऋ॒तं ह्य।᳡स्या॒मार्पि॑त॒मपि॒ ब्रह्मा॑थो॒ तपः॑ ॥
items.pada_patha: ब्रा॒ह्म॒णेभ्य॑: । व॒शाम् । द॒त्वा । सर्वा॑न् । लो॒कान् । सम् । अ॒श्नु॒ते॒ । ऋ॒तम् । हि । अ॒स्या॒म् । आर्पि॑तम् । अपि॑ । ब्रह्म॑ । अथो॒ इति॑ । तप॑: ॥१०.३३॥

commentaries.whitney: Having given the cow to the Brahmans, one attains all worlds; for righteousness is set in her, also bráhman , likewise penance.
commentaries.whitney_notes: Ppp. reads in a vaçā dattvā brāh- , and in c āhitam instead of ārpitam .

items.samhita_patha_plain: ब्राह्मणेभ्यो वशां दत्त्वा सर्वांल्लोकान्त्समश्नुते। ऋतं ह्य।᳡स्यामार्पितमपि ब्रह्माथो तपः ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: ब्राह्मणेभ्य: । वशाम् । दत्वा । सर्वान् । लोकान् । सम् । अश्नुते । ऋतम् । हि । अस्याम् । आर्पितम् । अपि । ब्रह्म । अथो इति । तप: ॥१०.३३॥

items.samhita_patha: व॒शां दे॒वा उप॑ जीवन्ति व॒शां म॑नु॒ष्या᳡ उ॒त। व॒शेदं सर्व॑मभव॒द्याव॒त्सूर्यो॑ वि॒पश्य॑ति ॥

commentaries.whitney: On the cow the gods subsist; on the cow, men also; the cow became this all, so far as the sun looks abroad.
commentaries.whitney_notes: The Anukr. takes no notice of the redundant syllable in a (read, by irregular combination, devó ’pa ). ⌊Here ends the fifth anuvāka , with 2 hymns and 61 verses. The quoted Anukr. says, referring to this last hymn, catasraḥ (i.e. 4 over 30).⌋ ⌊One ms. (P.) sums up the verses aright as 350.⌋ ⌊Here ends the twenty-third prapāṭhaka .⌋

items.samhita_patha_plain: वशां देवा उप जीवन्ति वशां मनुष्या᳡ उत। वशेदं सर्वमभवद्यावत्सूर्यो विपश्यति ॥
items.pada_patha_plain: वशाम् । देवा: । उप । जीवन्ति । वशाम् । मनुष्या᳡: । उत । वशा । इदम्। सर्वम् । अभवत् । यावत् । सूर्य: । विऽपश्यति ॥१०.३४॥
